items.title: Base change of the naive cotangent complex is a quasi-isomorphism over a flat algebra, and derived base change works under a tor amplitude bound
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement concerns a cocartesian square of rings and says that if the algebra is flat over the base then the base change of its naive cotangent complex is a quasi-isomorphism onto the naive cotangent complex of the base changed algebra, and that the derived version holds as well when the naive cotangent complex has tor amplitude in the interval from minus one to zero (statement lines 22809-22823). The proof chooses a polynomial presentation, uses flatness to identify the kernels of the two presentations and hence the conormal modules, compares the modules of differentials to get an isomorphism of complexes, and then observes that a two-term complex whose degree zero term is free has the stated tor amplitude exactly when its conormal module is flat, which makes the ordinary and derived tensor products agree (proof lines 22825-22852). The identification of the conormal module under base change is what carries the argument. The counted span refers twice, once to a section of another chapter and once to a lemma of this chapter, both carried as navigation stubs.

primary.label: author lemma environment with its own label lemma-base-change-NL-flat (canonical tag 0FJU), with the Xy-pic cocartesian diagram and the two conclusions (source lines 22809-22823)
